extracted.intended_audience: researchers and prospective authors in numerical analysis / scientific computing
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the aims, scope, and publication expectations for submissions to the journal Numerische Mathematik, including topical coverage, quality/significance expectations, article type, and open‑access/publishing policy notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High quality and significance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerische Mathematik is committed to publishing exceptionally high-quality papers that unveil significant and groundbreaking advancements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal seeks work that is both of exceptional quality and that brings significant / groundbreaking advances to the field; submissions should meet both aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — numerical analysis in the most general sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal covers all facets of Numerical Analysis in its most general sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their work fits within the broad remit of Numerical Analysis; topics outside this remit are unlikely to be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core focus — conception and analysis of efficient numerical schemes used on computers
rubrics_metrics.description: The conception and mathematical analysis of efficient numerical schemes actually used on computers (the 'core' of Numerical Analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to contributions that develop and rigorously analyse numerical schemes with practical computational relevance (i.e., schemes actually used on computers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical coverage — optimization, control, modelling, and mathematical aspects of scientific computing
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimization and Control Theory; Mathematical Modeling; The mathematical aspects of Scientific Computing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions in these subareas are within the journal's remit; authors working in these domains should emphasise the mathematical/numerical-analysis contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research contributions (article type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Latest articles listed are labeled 'OriginalPaper', indicating the journal publishes original research papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit work that reports original theoretical or methodological advances rather than reviews or non‑original summaries; use the 'OriginalPaper' article type where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access / publication agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your institution has a Read and Publish (Springer Compact) agreement, you may publish your article open access — at no cost to you — in more than 1,850 Springer hybrid journals, including Numerische Mathematik.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check institutional agreements to determine OA eligibility and potential APC coverage; this is a procedural note about publishing options rather than a quality criterion.
